newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Volker seeks to keep gross margins over 3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Volker seeks to keep gross margins over 3 pct.

text.p: Construction group Volker Stevin said on Friday it would seek to maintain gross margins on completed work at more than three percent.
The group said earlier its gross profit margin -- measured as a proportion of turnover -- rose to 3.3 percent in 1996 from 2.8 percent a year earlier.
"It's quite an achievement to raise margins above three percent," Volker's finance director Pim Dijkman told a results news conference.
"We will try to maintain the increase (in 1997)," chairman Aad Baardewijk added.
Dijkman said Volker Stevin would give priority to profitability over turnover. "Low-margin business weakens the company," he said.
He said the first two months of 1997 had progressed well for the group, but declined further details.
Volker Stevin earlier reported 1996 net profits rose to 73 million guilders from a year-earlier 58 million and forecast further earnings growth in 1997.
